content: The European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 2015 schedule outlines a series of interviews and discussions with leading medical professionals, focusing on groundbreaking research and clinical trials in cardiology. Sunday, August 30, 2015 At 4:30 PM, Dr. Robert Byrne will provide a comprehensive wrap-up of ESC 2015, offering insights from the perspective of the UK and Ireland. Monday, August 31, 2015 At 8:30 AM, Dr. Vivek Reddy will discuss the safety and efficacy of a leadless pacemaker, presenting findings from the LEADLESS II clinical trial. The embargo on this topic lifts on Sunday, August 30th, at 5:38 PM. At 9:30 AM, Dr. Kazuaki Kaitani and Dr. Atsushi Kobori will present two studies: the EAST-AF trial, which evaluates the short-term use of antiarrhythmic drugs after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation, and the UNDER-ATP trial, which examines adenosine triphosphate-guided ablation for atrial fibrillation by unmasking dormant electrical reconduction. The embargo for both studies lifts on Sunday, August 30th, at 4:30 PM. At 10:00 AM, Professor Michel Ovize will discuss the CIRCUS trial, which investigates whether cyclosporine improves clinical outcomes in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th, at 12:27 PM. At 11:30 AM, Dr. Morris Brown will present the principal results of the PATHWAY-3 trial, which compares single and combination diuretics in the treatment of essential hypertension. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st, at 5:16 PM. At 12:00 PM, Dr. Luigi Di Biase will discuss the BELIEF trial, which examines the effect of empirical left atrial appendage isolation on long-term outcomes in patients with long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation undergoing catheter ablation. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th, at 4:53 PM. At 1:30 PM, Dr. Eldrin Lewis will present findings from the ELIXA trial, which evaluates the use of Lixisenatide in patients with acute coronary syndromes. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st, at 11:36 AM. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Dirk Westermann will discuss the use of a high-sensitivity Troponin I 1-hour algorithm for the accurate and rapid diagnosis of myocardial infarction. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th, at 11:00 AM. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Basil Lewis will provide a wrap-up of ESC 2015 in Hebrew. At 3:30 PM, Dr. Renato Lopes will provide a wrap-up of ESC 2015 in Portuguese. At 4:00 PM, Professor Freek Verheugt will provide a wrap-up of ESC 2015 from the perspective of the Netherlands. Tuesday, September 1, 2015 At 9:30 AM, Dr. Takeshi Kimura will present the ABSORB Japan trial, which evaluates the 12-month clinical and 13-month angiographic outcomes of the Absorb Bioresorbable Vascular Scaffold compared to metallic drug-eluting stents. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st, at 5:06 PM. At 10:00 AM, Dr. Gérard Helft will discuss the OPTIDUAL trial, which compares 12 months versus 48 months of clopidogrel therapy following drug-eluting stent placement. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st, at 12:12 PM. At 10:30 AM, Dr. Pamela Douglas will present the results of the PLATFORM study, which evaluates the outcomes of an FFRCT diagnostic strategy compared to usual care in patients with suspected coronary artery disease. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st, at 4:30 PM. At 11:00 AM, Dr. Hisao Ogawa will discuss the ATTEMPT-CVD trial, which investigates the use of Telmisartan for the prevention of cardiovascular diseases, alongside a wrap-up of ESC 2015 in Japanese. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st, at 4:30 PM. At 11:30 AM, Dr. Marco Valgimigli will present the MATRIX Antithrombin study, which focuses on minimizing adverse hemorrhagic events through transradial access and systemic implementation of angioX. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st, at 5:24 PM. At 12:00 PM, Professor Thomas MacDonald will discuss the SCOT trial, which compares the cardiovascular safety of celecoxib to traditional non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st, at 11:54 AM. At 1:00 PM, Dr. Gregg Stone will present findings on peri-infarct zone pacing as a strategy to prevent adverse left ventricular remodeling in patients with very large myocardial infarctions. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th, at 11:54 AM. At 1:30 PM, Dr. Patrick Serruys will discuss the ABSORB STEMI TROFI II trial, which compares everolimus-eluting bioresorbable vascular scaffolds to durable polymer everolimus-eluting metallic stents in patients with acute myocardial infarction. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st, at 4:48 PM. At 2:00 PM, Dr. Frank Rademakers will present research on determining optimal non-invasive parameters for predicting left ventricular morphologic and functional remodeling in patients with chronic ischemic conditions. The embargo lifts on Sunday, August 30th, at 11:18 AM. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Gerasimos Filippatos will discuss the ARTS-HF trial, which compares finerenone to eplerenone in patients with worsening chronic heart failure and type 2 diabetes mellitus and/or chronic kidney disease. The embargo lifts on Monday, August 31st, at 11:18 AM. At 3:30 PM, Dr. Carlos A. Morillo will present findings from the BENznidazole Evaluation For Interrupting Trypanosomiasis (BENEFIT) trial. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 1st, at 12:08 PM. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Stefan James, joined by Dr. Jonas Oldgren, will provide a wrap-up of ESC 2015 from a Scandinavian perspective. At 4:30 PM, Dr. Sergio Leonardi, joined by Professor Gaetano De Ferrari, will provide a wrap-up of ESC 2015 in Italian. From 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM, Professor Gilles Montalescot will discuss the ALBATROSS trial, which evaluates early aldosterone blockade in acute myocardial infarction, and the AEGEAN study, which assesses an education and guidance program for apixaban adherence in non-valvular atrial fibrillation. He will also provide a wrap-up of ESC 2015 in French. The embargo for ALBATROSS lifts on Sunday, August 30th, at 11:36 AM, and the embargo for AEGEAN lifts on Sunday, August 30th, at 5:16 PM. Wednesday, September 2, 2015 At 9:00 AM, Professor Harvey White will provide a wrap-up of ESC 2015 from the perspective of the Pacific Rim. At 9:30 AM, Professor Sigmund Silber will provide a wrap-up of ESC 2015 in German.
